optimized_sql:
WITH aug_returns AS (
    SELECT sr.sr_item_sk,
           sr.sr_ticket_number,
           sr.sr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_returned_date_sk
    FROM store_returns sr
    WHERE sr.sr_returned_date_sk BETWEEN
          (SELECT MIN(d.d_date_sk) FROM date_dim d WHERE d.d_year = 2001 AND d.d_moy = 8)
          AND
          (SELECT MAX(d.d_date_sk) FROM date_dim d WHERE d.d_year = 2001 AND d.d_moy = 8)
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM date_dim d2
          WHERE d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
            AND d2.d_year = 2001
            AND d2.d_moy = 8
      )
),
sales_lag AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_store_sk,
           CASE
               WHEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk IS NULL THEN 0
               WHEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 30 THEN 1
               WHEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 60 THEN 2
               WHEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 90 THEN 3
               WHEN sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 120 THEN 4
               ELSE 5
           END AS bucket,
           COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM aug_returns sr
    JOIN store_sales ss
      ON ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
    JOIN date_dim d1
      ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
    GROUP BY ss.ss_store_sk, bucket
)
SELECT st.s_store_name,
       st.s_company_id,
       st.s_street_number,
       st.s_street_name,
       st.s_street_type,
       st.s_suite_number,
       st.s_city,
       st.s_county,
       st.s_state,
       st.s_zip,
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 1 THEN b.cnt ELSE 0 END)::bigint AS "30 days",
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 2 THEN b.cnt ELSE 0 END)::bigint AS "31-60 days",
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 3 THEN b.cnt ELSE 0 END)::bigint AS "61-90 days",
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 4 THEN b.cnt ELSE 0 END)::bigint AS "91-120 days",
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 5 THEN b.cnt ELSE 0 END)::bigint AS ">120 days"
FROM sales_lag b
JOIN store st
  ON b.ss_store_sk = st.s_store_sk
GROUP BY st.s_store_name,
         st.s_company_id,
         st.s_street_number,
         st.s_street_name,
         st.s_street_type,
         st.s_suite_number,
         st.s_city,
         st.s_county,
         st.s_state,
         st.s_zip
ORDER BY st.s_store_name,
         st.s_company_id,
         st.s_street_number,
         st.s_street_name,
         st.s_street_type,
         st.s_suite_number,
         st.s_city,
         st.s_county,
         st.s_state,
         st.s_zip
LIMIT 100

PARTIAL MONTH-COVERING INDEX — TARGET: `store_returns.sr_returned_date_sk` and its join columns — TRANSFORMATION: rewrite the `date_dim d2` join as an explicit August-2001 `sr_returned_date_sk` range, and add a covering partial B-tree on `(sr_item_sk, sr_ticket_number, sr_customer_sk)` for that range, so only the qualifying month of `store_returns` is read and it is read index-only.

2. TWO-STAGE BUCKET PRE-AGGREGATION — TARGET: final GROUP BY/ORDER BY over the ten `s_*` store text columns — TRANSFORMATION: in an inner step compute the day-difference bucket per matched row and aggregate counts by `(ss_store_sk, bucket)`; then join `store` and pivot the bucket counts into the five `sum(case...)` columns, shrinking the final wide sort/group from millions of rows to at most `#stores × 5` rows.

3. COVERING INDEX-ONLY PROBE INTO STORE_SALES — TARGET: `store_sales` primary-key lookup via `(ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number)` — TRANSFORMATION: add a covering B-tree on those two key columns that also carries `ss_customer_sk`, `ss_sold_date_sk`, and `ss_store_sk`, so every probe from `store_returns` fetches the needed sale data from the index without touching the 57.6M-row heap.

4. RESIDUALIZE CUSTOMER EQUALITY — TARGET: fact join condition `ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: use `(ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number)` as the unique lookup key for the `store_sales`/`store_returns` match and apply `customer_sk` equality as a residual filter on the single fetched candidate, reducing the join key from three integers to two.
